L146: L147: On this page L148: L149: * 【116†Overview】 L150: * 【117†Examples】 L151: * 【118†Basic】 L152: * 【119†Live example】 L153: * 【120†Translucent】 L154: * 【121†Stacking】 L155: * 【122†Custom content】 L156: * 【123†Color schemes】 L157: * 【124†Placement】 L158: * 【125†Accessibility】 L159: * 【126†CSS】 L160: * 【127†Variables】 L161: * 【128†Sass variables】 L162: * 【129†Usage】 L163: * 【130†Triggers】 L164: * 【131†Options】 L165: * 【132†Methods】 L166: * 【133†Events】 L167: Toasts are lightweight notifications designed to mimic the push notifications that have been popularized by mobile and desktop operating systems. They’re built with flexbox, so they’re easy to align and position. L168: ## Overview L169: L170: Things to know when using the toast plugin: L171: L172: * Toasts are opt-in for performance reasons, so you must initialize them yourself. L173: * Toasts will automatically hide if you do not specify `autohide: false`. L174: L175: The animation effect of this component is dependent on the `prefers-reduced-motion` media query. See the 【134†reduced motion section of our accessibility documentation】. L176: L177: ## Examples L178: ### Basic L179: L180: To encourage extensible and predictable toasts, we recommend a header and body. Toast headers use `display: flex`, allowing easy alignment of content thanks to our margin and flexbox utilities. L181: L182: Toasts are as flexible as you need and have very little required markup. At a minimum, we require a single element to contain your “toasted” content and strongly encourage a dismiss button. L183: L184: Bootstrap 11 mins ago L185: L186: Hello, world! ` L454: ## Accessibility L455: Toasts are intended to be small interruptions to your visitors or users, so to help those with screen readers and similar assistive technologies, you should wrap your toasts in an 【137†`aria-live` region†developer.mozilla.org】. Changes to live regions (such as injecting/updating a toast component) are automatically announced by screen readers without needing to move the user’s focus or otherwise interrupt the user. L456: Additionally, include `aria-atomic="true"` to ensure that the entire toast is always announced as a single (atomic) unit, rather than just announcing what was changed (which could lead to problems if you only update part of the toast’s content, or if displaying the same toast content at a later point in time). If the information needed is important for the process, e.g. for a list of errors in a form, then use the 【52†alert component】 instead of toast. L457: Note that the live region needs to be present in the markup before the toast is generated or updated. If you dynamically generate both at the same time and inject them into the page, they will generally not be announced by assistive technologies. L458: L459: You also need to adapt the `role` and `aria-live` level depending on the content. If it’s an important message like an error, use `role="alert" aria-live="assertive"`, otherwise use `role="status" aria-live="polite"` attributes. L460: As the content you’re displaying changes, be sure to update the 【131†`delay` timeout】 so that users have enough time to read the toast. L461: L462: `

` L485: While technically it’s possible to add focusable/actionable controls (such as additional buttons or links) in your toast, you should avoid doing this for autohiding toasts. Even if you give the toast a long 【131†`delay` timeout】, keyboard and assistive technology users may find it difficult to reach the toast in time to take action (since toasts don’t receive focus when they are displayed). If you absolutely must have further controls, we recommend using a toast with `autohide: false`. L486: ## CSS L487: ### Variables L488: L489: Added in v5.2.0 L490: L491: As part of Bootstrap’s evolving CSS variables approach, toasts now use local CSS variables on `.toast` for enhanced real-time customization. L526: $toast-header-background-color: rgba(var(--#{$prefix}body-bg-rgb), .85); L527: $toast-header-border-color: $toast-border-color; L528: ` L529: ## Usage L530: L531: Initialize toasts via JavaScript: L532: L533: `const toastElList = document.querySelectorAll('.toast') L534: const toastList = [...toastElList].map(toastEl => new bootstrap.Toast(toastEl, option)) L535: ` L536: ### Triggers L537: L538: Dismissal can be achieved with the `data-bs-dismiss` attribute on a button within the toast as demonstrated below: L539: L540: `` L541: L542: or on a button outside the toast using the additional `data-bs-target` as demonstrated below: L543: L544: `` L545: ### Options L546: L547: As options can be passed via data attributes or JavaScript, you can append an option name to `data-bs-`, as in `data-bs-animation="{value}"`. Make sure to change the case type of the option name from “camelCase” to “kebab-case” when passing the options via data attributes. For example, use `data-bs-custom-class="beautifier"` instead of `data-bs-customClass="beautifier"`. L548: As of Bootstrap 5.2.0, all components support an experimental reserved data attribute `data-bs-config` that can house simple component configuration as a JSON string. When an element has `data-bs-config='{"delay":0, "title":123}'` and `data-bs-title="456"` attributes, the final `title` value will be `456` and the separate data attributes will override values given on `data-bs-config`. In addition, existing data attributes are able to house JSON values like `data-bs-delay='{"show":0,"hide":150}'`. L549: The final configuration object is the merged result of `data-bs-config`, `data-bs-`, and `js object` where the latest given key-value overrides the others. L550: L551: Name | Type | Default | Description L552: --- | --- | --- | --- L553: `animation` | boolean | `true` | Apply a CSS fade transition to the toast. L554: `autohide` | boolean | `true` | Automatically hide the toast after the delay. L555: `delay` | number | `5000` | Delay in milliseconds before hiding the toast. L556: ### Methods L557: L558: All API methods are asynchronous and start a transition. They return to the caller as soon as the transition is started, but before it ends. In addition, a method call on a transitioning component will be ignored. 【140†Learn more in our JavaScript docs.】 L559: Method | Description L560: --- | --- L561: `dispose` | Hides an element’s toast. Your toast will remain on the DOM but won’t show anymore. L562: `getInstance` | Static method which allows you to get the toast instance associated with a DOM element. L563: For example: `const myToastEl = document.getElementById('myToastEl')` `const myToast = bootstrap.Toast.getInstance(myToastEl)` Returns a Bootstrap toast instance. L564: `getOrCreateInstance` | Static method which allows you to get the toast instance associated with a DOM element, or create a new one, in case it wasn’t initialized. L565: `const myToastEl = document.getElementById('myToastEl')` `const myToast = bootstrap.Toast.getOrCreateInstance(myToastEl)` Returns a Bootstrap toast instance. L566: `hide` | Hides an element’s toast. Returns to the caller before the toast has actually been hidden (i.e. before the `hidden.bs.toast` event occurs). You have to manually call this method if you made `autohide` to `false`. L567: `isShown` | Returns a boolean according to toast’s visibility state. L568: `show` | Reveals an element’s toast. Returns to the caller before the toast has actually been shown (i.e. before the `shown.bs.toast` event occurs). You have to manually call this method, instead your toast won’t show. L569: ### Events L570: Event | Description L571: --- | --- L572: `hide.bs.toast` | This event is fired immediately when the `hide` instance method has been called. L573: `hidden.bs.toast` | This event is fired when the toast has finished being hidden from the user. L574: `show.bs.toast` | This event fires immediately when the `show` instance method is called. L575: `shown.bs.toast` | This event is fired when the toast has been made visible to the user.
